contract.purpose: Compute directed maximum s-t flow, inspect per-edge flows, and extract residual reachability for a minimum cut.

contract.output: Insertion-order edge IDs; flow returns additional augmented flow; edge accessors expose capacity/current flow; min_cut returns residual-reachable vertices.
contract.preconditions: n >= 2 for solving; distinct valid s,t; nonnegative capacities and flow limit. This integration uses n,m <= 100000000, with 2*m residual edges representable. Self/parallel/antiparallel edges are valid.
contract.indexing: Vertices [0,n); edge IDs [0,m) in insertion order; min_cut has n Boolean entries.
contract.time: Build O(n+m); flow O(n^2*m) general bound or O(F*(n+m)); get_edge O(1), edges O(m), min_cut O(n+m).

contract.mutation: flow mutates residual capacities. Repeated calls with the same source and sink are supported and return only new augmentation, not the cumulative value.
contract.global_state: No mutable algorithm globals.
contract.recursion: Augmenting DFS is recursive and can use O(n) stack depth.
contract.limitations: min_cut is always residual reachability, but is an s-t minimum-cut certificate only after exhausting augmentations; reaching a flow limit is insufficient. Arbitrary change_edge edits are not exposed, since callers would need to preserve global flow feasibility.

entries.name: Ordered associative rerooting DP framework
entries.reason: Independent iterative framework supports noncommutative associative merges in exact input-adjacency order. contract.purpose: Compute an all-roots tree DP from an ordered associative merge, vertex finalization and directed edge-transfer callbacks, without requiring commutativity.
contract.input: toolkit::rerooting(n, undirected edge list, identity, merge, finish, transfer). merge(T,T)->T combines incoming values; finish(T,int vertex)->T includes the vertex; transfer(T,int from,int to)->T converts a neighbor-rooted state into an incoming contribution.
contract.output: vector<T> with one finalized state per possible root. At each vertex incoming neighbors are folded in edge insertion order, excluding the current parent, before finish; transfer receives the actual from/to orientation.
contract.preconditions: Nonempty simple connected tree with n-1 edges and vertices in [0,n). Invalid tree structure throws invalid_argument; bad endpoints throw out_of_range. contract.indexing: Zero-based vertices. Input edge insertion order determines each endpoint's neighbor order; original edge orientation does not affect adjacency ordering, but transfer direction is explicit.
contract.time: O(n) callback invocations and O(n) T copies/assignments under constant-size constant-cost state operations. Actual callback and value-copy costs are additional; string serialization may be quadratic overall.
contract.space: O(n) T objects plus O(n) validated tree/traversal storage; the bytes occupied by user states and callback allocations are additional.
contract.numeric_limits: int vertex indices. The framework does not perform arithmetic on T; callers must prevent overflow in merge/finish/transfer. The example's unweighted (count,distance-sum) long long state fits for int-sized trees.
contract.mutation: No mutation of caller edges or identity; local down/up/prefix/suffix states are independent per invocation. User callback side effects are outside the supported deterministic contract.
contract.global_state: None required; no framework globals.
contract.recursion: Iterative bottom-up and top-down passes, including validation; callbacks may have their own recursion requirements.
contract.limitations: Static nonempty trees only. Correct associativity, identity and semantics are caller obligations. entries.name: Seeded shared-context byte polynomial rolling hash
entries.reason: Repository-original implementation, explicitly not adapted from an upstream header or std::hash. Inspected Nyaan and Luzhiled rolling hashes use clock-seeded static bases; Suisen set_bases mutates shared static state and invalidates live hashes. An original immutable explicitly seeded context supplies the required independent lifetimes and reproducibility without modifying those sources.

contract.purpose: Provide constant-time normalized substring polynomial fingerprints as a randomized candidate filter, never an equality proof.
contract.input: Create shared_ptr<const toolkit::RollingHashContext>(seed), then toolkit::RollingHash(text,context). All bytes are encoded as unsigned byte+1. slice(left,right) and possibly_equal(left,right,other,other_left,other_right) use half-open ranges.
contract.output: slice returns Digest{value,length}; empty slices have value zero and length zero. possibly_equal returns equal lengths and equal field fingerprints, which may still represent unequal byte strings.
contract.preconditions: Context must be nonnull; invalid_argument otherwise. Cross-object possibly_equal requires the SAME shared context object, even if distinct contexts happen to have identical seed/base. Ranges must satisfy 0<=left<=right<=size; out_of_range otherwise. Prefix allocations must fit memory.
contract.indexing: Zero-based half-open substrings [left,right), including [size,size). Digest equality compares the stored length and value only; raw digests carry no context identity, so callers must not compare them across incompatible contexts.
contract.time: O(n) construction with constant-width modular arithmetic. O(1) slice and candidate comparison. Copying an index is O(n).
contract.space: O(n) prefix hashes and powers per index, plus an O(1) shared immutable context; returned Digest is O(1).
contract.numeric_limits: Prime modulus is 2^61-1. Base is sampled from [257,modulus-2] with mt19937_64 seeded by uint64_t and uniform_int_distribution. Products use unsigned __int128 below 2^122; additions remain below 2^62. size_t range and vector max_size checks avoid prefix-size overflow.
contract.mutation: Input is not retained or changed. Prefixes/powers and context are immutable after construction. Owning shared pointers keep contexts alive independently of caller references; moved-from indexes should only be destroyed or assigned.
contract.global_state: No shared mutable globals, clock, random_device or std::hash. Context generation uses a local explicitly seeded PRNG. Reproduction is guaranteed within the tested compiler/standard-library environment; uniform_int_distribution mappings are not a cross-library serialization format.
contract.recursion: Iterative construction/arithmetic; constant call stack.
contract.limitations: Single-field randomized hashing can collide; finite tests do not prove collision freedom. A public/fixed seed is predictable and offers no adversarial or cryptographic guarantee. Verify candidate matches by exact byte comparison when correctness requires certainty. There is no claimed universal collision probability for adaptive inputs or biased seed selection. Tests check direct substring-polynomial values with independent doubling modular multiplication and enforce only the no-false-negative implication for actual string equality.

entries.name: Immutable byte suffix automaton and substring counts
entries.reason: Integrates unchanged pinned Suisen CC0 SuffixAutomaton<char> through an independently authored immutable owning facade. The Nyaan candidate was rejected because it uses target(popcnt), a restricted bitmask alphabet and shared static sorted state. contract.purpose: Build an immutable suffix-automaton snapshot for substring membership, distinct nonempty substring count and overlapping occurrence counts.
contract.input: toolkit::SuffixAutomaton(const string&) builds from any byte string. contains(pattern) and occurrences(pattern) accept arbitrary byte patterns, including empty.
contract.output: contains reports exact substring membership. occurrences counts every overlapping start; empty occurs n+1 times at all boundaries, including for empty text. distinct_substrings counts distinct nonempty substrings and is zero for empty text.
contract.preconditions: Text length n must be <=(INT_MAX-1)/2; oversized input throws length_error. Enough memory for states, ordered transition maps and counter storage is required. Pattern lengths do not use narrowed indices in the exposed query methods.
contract.indexing: State IDs and suffix links are internal zero-based int indices and are not exposed by the facade. Empty-pattern boundaries conceptually range from 0 through n.
contract.time: O(n log(sigma+1)) construction for fixed byte alphabet sigma<=256, including suffix-automaton states and occurrence propagation; O(|pattern| log(sigma+1)) per membership/count query; O(1) cached distinct-count query. Copying the facade copies its O(n) counter vector.
contract.space: O(n) automaton and counter memory for fixed byte alphabet. Copies share immutable automaton ownership but have independent copied counter vectors.
contract.numeric_limits: State counts fit int under the checked bound; distinct count is at most n*(n+1)/2 and occurrence counts at most n+1, both within signed long long for this bound. Byte signedness does not affect equality/map correctness.
contract.mutation: Construction copies information out of the input; later input changes have no effect. The facade exposes no append, rebuild or mutable state. Copies remain usable after original facade/input destruction; moved-from objects should only be destroyed or assigned.
contract.global_state: No mutable algorithm globals. A shared_ptr<const Engine> retains the exact automaton address borrowed by Suisen's occurrence counter, even across facade copies and relocation.
contract.recursion: Exposed construction/count/membership use iterative upstream operations. Upstream recursive occurrence-enumeration APIs are not exposed or claimed by this facade.
contract.limitations: This is an immutable substring index, not an online append wrapper or a suffix-array replacement. Direct use of Suisen's borrowed counters requires their automaton to remain alive and unchanged. Tests use brute-force substring-frequency maps and direct pattern scans, including clone-heavy strings, full-byte queries and lifetime/copy checks.

entries.name: Deterministic unsigned 64-bit Miller-Rabin
entries.reason: Independently authored full-uint64 implementation. Inspected pinned KACTL MillerRabin.h and CC0 ModMulLL.h: the floating-point modular multiplication contract is narrower than uint64, so it is not reused. Uses exact GNU __uint128_t arithmetic and the standard seven deterministic witnesses.

contract.purpose: Decide primality deterministically over the entire unsigned 64-bit domain; expose exact modular multiplication and exponentiation prerequisites.
contract.input: is_prime_u64(uint64_t n); multiply_mod_u64(a,b,modulus); power_mod_u64(a,exponent,modulus), with all arguments uint64_t.
contract.output: Primality is false for 0 and 1 and true precisely for primes. Arithmetic returns a reduced residue; power uses 0^0=1 before reduction, including result 0 for every operation modulo 1.
contract.preconditions: Primality accepts every uint64_t without additional preconditions. Modular helpers require a positive modulus and throw invalid_argument for zero. Validate negative external inputs before unsigned conversion.
contract.indexing: No index API. The witness set is exactly 2,325,9375,28178,450775,9780504,1795265022; bases divisible by n are skipped.
contract.time: O(7 log n) modular multiplications for primality; O(1) multiplication and O(log(exponent+1)) exponentiation under fixed-width arithmetic.
contract.space: O(1) auxiliary storage.
contract.numeric_limits: All n,a,b,exponent in [0,UINT64_MAX] and moduli in [1,UINT64_MAX]. A uint64 product fits GNU __uint128_t exactly; no signed overflow, floating-point modular reduction, or long-double precision assumption.
contract.mutation: Inputs are passed by value; no caller-owned data changes.
contract.global_state: No mutable algorithm globals or randomness; base.hpp imports standard names.
contract.recursion: Iterative only.
contract.limitations: GNU C++17 with __uint128_t, not arbitrary precision or an unbounded-integer primality proof. Sieve/trial-division oracles cover small and seeded cases; independent complete-factorization Lucas certificates verify the two large prime fixtures, with pseudoprimes and constructed 64-bit composites covering adversarial edges. Modular arithmetic is independently checked by overflow-free repeated doubling.

notices: Independently authored local implementation and tests; no upstream implementation copied. The deterministic witness constants are mathematical algorithm parameters, not a copied header. No repository-wide license is assigned to local code.

entries.name: Seeded unsigned 64-bit Pollard rho with explicit failure
entries.reason: Independently authored bounded-retry Floyd rho and complete-factorization driver. Inspected pinned KACTL Factor.h/ModMulLL.h and Luzhiled fast-prime-factorization.hpp; their narrower arithmetic or unbounded retry/global-modulus behavior does not satisfy this integration's full-width seed/work/failure contract.

contract.purpose: Factor a positive uint64 into its complete prime multiset using deterministic primality classification and seeded randomized Pollard rho splitting.
contract.input: factor_u64(n,seed,RhoBudget{attempts_per_split,steps_per_attempt}); n and seed are uint64_t. Defaults are 32 attempts per composite split and 250000 Floyd steps per attempt.
contract.output: optional<vector<uint64_t>>: a present sorted complete prime multiset whose product is n, an empty vector for n=1, or nullopt if any split exhausts its budget. Failure never returns partial factors.
contract.preconditions: n>=1; zero throws invalid_argument. Budgets may be zero. Prime classification and trivial factors 2 or 3 do not consume rho steps. Allocation exceptions propagate separately from nullopt.
contract.indexing: Factors are sorted ascending and repeated with their multiplicity. One Floyd step evaluates the polynomial three times, then computes a gcd; attempts restart on a full-cycle gcd=n or step exhaustion.
contract.time: Successful rho splitting has heuristic expected O(sqrt(p)) iterations for a factor p under the usual random-polynomial model; gcd cost is additional. There is no worst-case bound on the work needed for successful factorization. Configured budgets cap total work at at most 63*A*S Floyd iterations plus at most 127 primality classifications and sorting at most 64 factors.
contract.space: O(log n) pending factors and output, bounded by the 64-bit input width, plus a fixed-size local mt19937_64 engine; no recursion stack.
contract.numeric_limits: All positive uint64_t n, including UINT64_MAX, high-bit primes and near-2^32 prime squares. Polynomial v*v+c fits __uint128_t; absolute differences use ordered unsigned subtraction. Seed supports every uint64_t.
contract.mutation: No input state changes. All partial factors are private and discarded on failure. To retry after nullopt, explicitly call with another seed and/or larger budget.
contract.global_state: No mutable globals. Each call resets local mt19937_64(seed); same input, seed and budget reproduce the same attempt sequence and failure result. Random parameters use documented modulo mapping, not cryptographic randomness.
contract.recursion: Iterative pending-factor stack.
contract.limitations: Finite budgets can fail, with no promised success probability or universal time bound. Parameter modulo mapping is slightly biased; expected runtime is not a deterministic guarantee. Independent trial-factorization and constructed-prime-factor oracles verify exact factors, primality and 128-bit product reconstruction; explicit zero-budget tests verify that partial results are never exposed. Not cryptographic side-channel-resistant code.

notices: Independently authored local Pollard rho, modular arithmetic, Miller-Rabin and tests. No copied upstream implementation and no new license assigned to local code. Inspected upstream implementations remain unchanged.

entries.name: Minimal non-coprime discrete logarithm for 32-bit moduli
entries.reason: Independently authored gcd stripping and ordered-map baby-step giant-step with minimal nonnegative exponent semantics. Inspected CC0 KACTL ModLog.h instead returns a positive exponent and uses signed products/unordered hashing; this integration makes zero, non-coprime inputs and the supported modulus bound explicit.

contract.purpose: Return the smallest nonnegative x solving a^x=b modulo m, including non-coprime bases and moduli.
contract.input: toolkit::discrete_log(uint64_t a,uint64_t b,uint64_t m); a and b are reduced internally.
contract.output: optional<uint64_t> minimal exponent, or nullopt if mathematically unsolvable. Modulus 1 always returns 0. With m>1, 0^0=1 gives log_0(1)=0, log_0(0)=1, and other residues have no solution.
contract.preconditions: 1<=m<=UINT32_MAX; zero and larger moduli throw invalid_argument instead of silently claiming arbitrary uint64 support. All uint64 a and b are valid. Memory allocation errors propagate, never masquerading as no solution.
contract.indexing: Exponents start at zero, not one. Gcd stripping checks each removed prefix; BSGS scans exponent blocks in increasing order and retains the largest baby index to select the smallest exponent within each block.
contract.time: O(sqrt(m) log(m+1)) time from ordered-map insert/find, plus logarithmic gcd stripping. No probabilistic hash-table performance assumption.
contract.space: O(sqrt(m)) map entries, at most 65536 baby-step insertions under the supported modulus limit.
contract.numeric_limits: m is bounded to 32 bits explicitly, while a,b and returned exponents use uint64_t. Products use __uint128_t modular helpers; block-index products fit uint64_t. Floating-point sqrt is corrected by exact integer comparisons before use.
contract.mutation: Only local reductions and map contents change; no caller data is modified.
contract.global_state: None. No PRNG, global modulus, or process-salted unordered container.
contract.recursion: None.
contract.limitations: Not an unrestricted 64-bit-modulus or cryptographic discrete-log solver. The precise bound controls memory rather than promising cheap arbitrary large-modulus searches. Exhaustive residue-orbit oracles cover all a,b for m<=60, seeded full-width a,b use small independent orbits, and near-UINT32_MAX known minimal powers and impossible/degenerate cases test the boundary.

notices: Independently authored gcd-stripping/BSGS implementation, modular helpers, examples and independent orbit tests. No upstream code copied; no new repository-wide license assigned.

entries.name: Dynamic square modular matrix exponentiation
entries.reason: Independently authored runtime-dimension/runtime-modulus implementation. Inspected pinned Luzhiled Matrix and SquareMatrix: their generic element arithmetic and dimension/initialization assumptions do not provide this explicit full-uint64 modular arithmetic, dimension rejection and exponent-zero contract.

contract.purpose: Multiply and exponentiate arbitrary-size square matrices over integers modulo an explicitly supplied positive modulus, without a fixed modulus or recurrence-specific template.
contract.input: ModMatrix is vector<vector<uint64_t>>. matrix_multiply_mod(a,b,modulus) and matrix_power_mod(matrix,uint64_t exponent,modulus). Entries may be unreduced.
contract.output: A fresh square matrix of reduced residues. Exponent 0 returns the modular identity, even for a zero matrix; modulo 1 this is all zeros. Empty matrices represent the supported 0x0 identity.
contract.preconditions: Every row must have the outer dimension, multiply operands must have equal dimensions, and modulus must be positive. Violations throw invalid_argument even when exponent is zero or dimensions are empty. Dimensions and allocations must fit available memory; allocation exceptions propagate.
contract.indexing: Zero-based [row][column]; conventional row-by-column product. Only square matrices are exposed, including 0x0; rectangular and ragged matrices are rejected.
contract.time: Multiplication O(n^3); exponentiation O(n^2 + n^3 log(exponent+1)), with exponent 0 requiring only validation and identity construction.
contract.space: O(n^2) matrices and temporary products; input to exponentiation is copied, not borrowed.
contract.numeric_limits: Entries and exponents may be UINT64_MAX; modulus is in [1,UINT64_MAX]. Each uint64 product plus one already-reduced accumulator fits __uint128_t, and reduction occurs for every term, so dimension does not accumulate an overflowing integer sum.
contract.mutation: No caller matrix is changed. The by-value power argument is normalized and squared locally.
contract.global_state: No global modulus, arithmetic type state, or macros; separate concurrent calls may use unrelated moduli.
contract.recursion: Iterative binary exponentiation and matrix loops.
contract.limitations: GNU __uint128_t is required. This is modular square-matrix arithmetic, not matrix inversion, negative powers, floating-point matrices, arbitrary rings or a fast asymptotic multiplication implementation. Independent repeated multiplication uses add/double modular products rather than the implementation's 128-bit product; full-width exponents are additionally checked against permutation-cycle and diagonal oracles.

notices: Independently authored local implementation and oracle tests; no upstream matrix code copied or altered. No repository-wide license is assigned to local code.

entries.name: Exact bounded-integer closed-segment intersection predicate
entries.reason: Repository-original wide-integer predicate. Inspected KACTL SegmentIntersection returns truncated coordinates for nonintegral crossings with integral Point and uses triple products; the requested exact predicate is implemented independently without copying that coordinate-returning routine or share-alike article code.

contract.purpose: Decide exactly whether two closed planar integer-coordinate segments have any common point.
contract.input: toolkit::segments_intersect(a,b,c,d) with toolkit::IntegerPoint{x,y}; endpoints a,b and c,d may coincide, and endpoint order is arbitrary.
contract.output: Boolean true for proper crossings, touching endpoints, collinear overlap and intersecting degenerate point-segments; false for disjoint closed sets.
contract.preconditions: Every coordinate must lie in [-1000000000000000000,1000000000000000000]. All four points are checked and out_of_range is thrown before arithmetic if any coordinate is invalid.
contract.indexing: No indexed container or half-open geometry: both endpoints belong to each segment. The two segment roles and each segment's orientation are interchangeable.
contract.time: O(1) orientation and bounding-interval tests.
contract.space: O(1) auxiliary storage.
contract.numeric_limits: Stored coordinates use signed long long. Subtractions are promoted to signed __int128 before evaluation; differences are at most 2e18 and cross determinants at most 8e36, below 2^127-1. Only signs are multiplied, never full determinants.
contract.mutation: All endpoints are passed by value; no caller data is modified.
contract.global_state: No mutable globals or upstream dependencies.
contract.recursion: No recursion; constant stack.
contract.limitations: This deliberately scoped API returns only intersection existence, not a rational intersection coordinate or overlap endpoints. There is no floating-point tolerance and no unbounded-int64 coordinate promise. Tests independently solve rational line parameters, handle parallel projection intervals and exhaustively check all endpoint quadruples on a 3-by-3 integer grid.

contract.space: O(n) converted Point<__int128> storage; upstream predicate itself uses O(1) auxiliary storage.

entries.name: Bounded-integer planar closest pair
entries.reason: Integrates unchanged explicitly CC0 KACTL ClosestPair and Point, using its actual ordered-set sweep rather than a quadratic substitute. contract.purpose: Find positions belonging to two distinct input entries with minimum exact squared Euclidean distance using an O(n log n) plane sweep.
contract.input: toolkit::closest_pair(const vector<IntegerPoint>& points) accepts empty inputs, unsorted points, duplicate coordinates and collinear sets.
contract.output: optional<ClosestPair> with first, second and squared_distance. Fewer than two entries give nullopt after validation. Duplicate entries can form a zero-distance pair even though their positions are equal.
contract.preconditions: Each coordinate must lie in [-100000000,100000000], checked for every point including singleton input; out_of_range otherwise. Input count must be below INT_MAX; length_error otherwise. Allocations must fit memory.
contract.indexing: Returned endpoints are coordinate values, not original indices. They represent distinct entries, so equal endpoints require duplicate occurrences in the input. No unique or lexicographically prescribed tie result is promised.
contract.time: O(n log n): sort by y, ordered-set insert/erase/range lookup and packing-bounded candidate scans inside the current-distance strip. No repeated full scan or sorting inside divide-and-conquer. Duplicate coordinates yield zero and collapse in the active set.
contract.space: O(n) converted/copy input and active ordered set.
contract.numeric_limits: |coordinate|<=1e8 implies squared pair distance <=8e16, strictly below LLONG_MAX used by unchanged upstream initialization. Differences and squared products fit signed long long. Upstream sqrt is used only to choose an expanded integer search window, not to return or compare a floating-point distance; independent test distances are evaluated in signed __int128.
contract.mutation: Caller input is unchanged; sorting and active-set updates affect only local owned values.
contract.global_state: No mutable globals. Unchanged KACTL exposes global Point, P=Point<long long>, closest and prelude aliases/macros; standalone compilation isolates its names.
contract.recursion: The sweep is iterative; std::sort may use O(log n) implementation stack. There is no linear-depth algorithm recursion.
contract.limitations: Coordinates outside the checked bound are intentionally unsupported; this adapter does not pretend to widen arithmetic inside the unchanged header. Raw ClosestPair.h requires at least two points and conflicts with the P=Point<double> alias in InsidePolygon's SegmentDistance dependency when combined without isolation. Non-inline upstream definitions require deliberate translation-unit handling. Tests use exhaustive pair enumeration, exact wide squared distances, duplicate identity checks and 100000-point vertical/duplicate structural cases.

entries.name: Finite normal-play subtraction-game Grundy values and moves
entries.reason: Independently authored finite-state mex dynamic programming with single-heap and disjoint-sum winning-move APIs. No upstream implementation is claimed for this previously missing integration.

contract.purpose: Precompute Sprague-Grundy values for a finite maximum heap size under a fixed subtraction set, and select winning moves in one heap or a disjoint sum.
contract.input: SubtractionGame(size_t maximum,vector<size_t> allowed); grundy(heap), winning_move(heap), nim_sum(vector<size_t> heaps), winning_move(vector<size_t> heaps).
contract.output: grundy returns mex of legal successor values. Single-heap winning_move returns the smallest legal removal reaching Grundy 0, or nullopt. Multiheap winning_move returns SubtractionMove{heap,removed}, choosing first heap then smallest removal reaching total XOR 0, or nullopt. nim_sum is the XOR of per-heap Grundy values.
contract.preconditions: Normal play: remove one allowed positive amount from exactly one heap, and no legal move loses. Zero removal throws invalid_argument; duplicates are ignored. Every queried heap must lie in [0,maximum], otherwise out_of_range. maximum=SIZE_MAX throws length_error before maximum+1 can overflow. State arrays must fit available memory.
contract.indexing: Heaps are inclusive 0..maximum. SubtractionMove.heap is a zero-based vector index and removed is the positive amount, not the remaining size. Moves larger than maximum are valid but never legal; empty move sets and empty heap vectors are valid losing games.
contract.time: Construction O(K log(K+1) + (maximum+1)*(K+1)), with K the number of supplied moves; deduplication can reduce the inner bound. grundy O(1), single winning move O(K+1), nim_sum O(H), multiheap winning move O(H*(K+1)) for H heaps.
contract.space: O(maximum+K+1) retained values/moves and constructor mex marks; queries use O(1) auxiliary storage.
contract.numeric_limits: Heap sizes and moves are size_t; maximum+1 is checked before allocation. Grundy values are at most the number of distinct legal move amounts. Huge move amounts including SIZE_MAX are harmless when larger than the queried heap.
contract.mutation: Construction takes and normalizes its own move vector. Queries are const and do not modify heap vectors; caller applies a returned removal.
contract.global_state: No mutable globals, PRNG or shared precomputation.
contract.recursion: Implementation uses iterative finite DP. Only independent small-state tests use recursive game-tree/mex oracles.
contract.limitations: Not misere play, infinite-state periodicity extrapolation, arbitrary impartial games, or heap-specific subtraction sets. Precomputation is linear in the finite heap bound times move count. Tests exhaust all subsets of removals 1..6 for heaps 0..30 and independently explore seeded multiheap game trees, including duplicate/oversized moves and invalid queries.

notices: Independently authored local finite subtraction-game implementation and oracle tests; no upstream code or educational prose copied and no upstream license invented. No repository-wide license has been selected for local code.

contract.purpose: Choose a subset with maximum exact signed sum not exceeding a signed bound, with explicit infeasibility and reconstruction.
contract.input: meet_in_middle_subset(vector<long long> values,long long limit).
contract.output: optional<SubsetOptimum> with signed __int128 sum and unsigned long long input-index mask; nullopt if no subset is feasible. Equal optima choose the numerically smallest mask.
contract.preconditions: At most 40 items or length_error. Arbitrary signed-64 values and signed-64 limit are allowed.
contract.indexing: Each input item is usable once; mask bit i selects values[i]. Empty subset is allowed but feasible only when 0<=limit; negative limits never silently default to the empty subset.
contract.time: O(n*2^ceil(n/2)), dominated by sorting and binary searches of half-subset sums.
contract.space: O(2^ceil(n/2)) wide sum/mask pairs; n=40 may require tens of MiB and allocation failures propagate.
contract.numeric_limits: All subset sums and search differences have magnitude at most 41*2^63, safely inside signed __int128. Masks use only bits 0..39; shifts are bounded.
contract.mutation: Input unchanged; half-subset arrays sorted/deduplicated locally.
contract.global_state: None.
contract.recursion: Subset generation iterative; standard sort may use O(n) stack in terms of original item count.
contract.limitations: Exact bounded-size subset-sum optimization, not a weight/value knapsack, approximate search or arbitrary-N solver.
